source_text: siquidem a primordio rerum conditor harum cum ipsis pariter compertus est, ipsis ad hoc prolatis, ut deus cognosceretur. I nec enim si aliquanto posterior Moyses primus uidetur in templo litterarum suarum deum mundi dedicasse, idcirco a Pentateucho natales agnitionis supputabuntur, cum totus Moysei stilus notitiam creatoris non instituat, sed a primordio enarret, a paradiso et Adam, non ab Aegypto et Moyse recensendam, denique maior popularitas generis humani, ne nominis quidem Moysei compotes, nedum instrumenti, deum Moysei tamen norunt; etiam tantam idolatria dominationem obumbrante, seorsum tamen illum quasi proprio nomine deum') perhibent et \'deum deorum\' et \'si deus dederit\' et \'quod deo placet\' et \'deo commendo.\' uide, an nouerint quem omnia posse testantur. nec hoc ullis Moysei libris debent. ante anima quam prophetia. animae enim a primordio conscientia dei dos est; eadem nec alia et in Aegyptiis et in Syris et in Ponticis. [Iudaeorum enim deum dicunt animae deum.] noli, barbare haeretice, priorem Abraham constituere quam mundum. et si unius familiae deus fuisset creator, tamen posterior tuo non erat, etiam Ponticis ante eum notus. accipiat igitur ab antecessore formam, a certo incertus, a cognito incognitus: numquam deus latebit, numquam deus deerit, semper intellegetur, semper audietur, etiam uidebitur, quomodo uolet. habet deus testimonia: totum hoc quod sumus et in quo sumus. sic probatur et deus et unus, dum non ignoratur, alio adhuc probari laborante.
pass_a_gloss: For indeed from the beginning of things the founder of these things is found together with them, these things having been brought forth so that God might be known. And not even if Moses seems to be somewhat later, the first in the temple of his writings to have dedicated the God of the world, for this reason the birthdays of recognition will be calculated from the Pentateuch, since the whole style of Moses does not establish the knowledge of the creator, but narrates from the beginning, from paradise and Adam, not from Egypt and Moses to be reckoned, finally the greater popularity of the human race, not even having the name of Moses, nonetheless know the God of Moses; and even with such great idolatry dominating, they nonetheless call him, as it were, by his own name, God, and 'God of gods' and 'if God gives' and 'what pleases God' and 'I commend to God.' See, whether they know the one who they testify is able to do all things. Nor do they owe this to any books of Moses. Before prophecy, the soul. For to the soul, from the beginning, the knowledge of God is given; and this same knowledge is not different, even among the Egyptians and the Syrians and the Pontics. For they call the God of the Jews the God of the soul. Do not, barbarous heretic, constitute Abraham as prior to the world. And if the creator had been the God of one family, nonetheless he was not later than you, even the Pontics knew him before him. Therefore, let him receive form from the predecessor, from the certain the uncertain, from the known the unknown: never will God be hidden, never will God be lacking, always he will be understood, always he will be heard, and even seen, however he wishes. God has testimonies: the whole of this which we are and in which we are. Thus God is proven and one, while he is not ignored, with another still laboring to prove.
pass_b_english: From the very beginning of creation, the Founder of all things has been discovered right alongside them, because they were brought into existence precisely so that God might be known. Even if Moses appears somewhat later as the first to dedicate the God of the world in the temple of his writings, that does not mean the birthday of this knowledge should be dated from the Pentateuch. Moses' entire style does not institute the knowledge of the Creator; it narrates that knowledge from the beginning — from Paradise and Adam, not from Egypt and Moses. The vast majority of the human race, who never even heard the name of Moses, let alone read his books, still know the God of Moses. And even under the blinding domination of idolatry, they nonetheless call him, as it were, by his own proper name — God — and 'God of gods,' and 'if God gives,' and 'what pleases God,' and 'I commend to God.' Look and see whether they know the one they testify is able to do all things. They owe this knowledge to no books of Moses. The soul comes before prophecy. For from the beginning, the knowledge of God is a gift given to the soul; and this same knowledge is no different among Egyptians, Syrians, and Pontics. (They call the God of the Jews the God of the soul.) Do not, you barbarous heretic, set Abraham up as prior to the world. And even if the Creator had been the God of only one family, he still would not be later than you; the Pontics knew him before Abraham did. So let the later receive form from the earlier, the uncertain from the certain, the unknown from the known. God will never be hidden, God will never be absent; he will always be understood, always be heard, and even be seen, however he wishes. God has his witnesses: this whole reality — what we are and the world we live in. Thus God is proven, and proven one, while he is not ignored, even though another still labors to prove him.
